name: Battle of Bibracte
intro: Near Bibracte in central Gaul, in June 58 BC, the first great battle of Caesar’s Gallic War. You are Julius Caesar, with six legions and about 4,000 allied cavalry. The Helvetii are migrating west with their families and wagons; Caesar claims 92,000 fighting men, modern estimates range from 12,000 to about 50,000.
debrief: In reality, short of grain, Caesar turned toward the Aeduan town of Bibracte; the Helvetii followed and attacked his rearguard. Caesar sent his cavalry to delay them and formed four veteran legions in three lines on a hillside, with the two new legions and the allies on top. The Helvetii advanced in close order behind their shields; Roman pila halted them and the legions charged downhill, driving them back. The Boii and Tulingi, about 15,000 strong, then struck the Roman flank, and Caesar turned his third line to face them while the first two pressed on. The fighting at the Helvetii wagons went on into the night, and the baggage and children of their leader Orgetorix were taken. Caesar’s figures for the Helvetii are disputed. The other choices are what-ifs.

win: The Helvetii are driven to their wagons.
The laager falls in the night.

decisions.title: Short of grain
decisions.text: You are Julius Caesar, governor of Gaul, shadowing the migrating Helvetii. Your grain has run low. The Aedui have not sent what they promised. Bibracte, their chief town, is a day’s march away.

hint.text: Dumnorix of the Aedui is said to be delaying the grain.

scout.text: A hungry army cannot fight. Turn toward Bibracte to feed the men, even if it means breaking contact.

fx.text: The army turns off toward Bibracte. The Helvetii, thinking you are retreating, turn to follow and attack.
The men march on empty stomachs.

choices.label: Halt and wait for the Aedui

decisions.title: The rearguard is attacked
decisions.text: The Helvetii fall on your rearguard. You need time to form the army.

scout.text: Send the cavalry to hold them off while the legions form on the hillside: veterans in three lines on the slope, the new legions and allies on top.

choices.label: Cavalry holds them while the legions form

fx.text: Your cavalry delays the Helvetii. The four veteran legions form three lines on the slope; the two new legions and the allies hold the top with the baggage.

choices.label: Turn and fight on the march before they gather strength

fx.text: The army fights in column, in disorder.

decisions.title: The shield wall
decisions.text: The Helvetii come uphill in a dense mass behind a wall of overlapping shields.

scout.text: Pila thrown into overlapping shields pin them together. Then charge downhill with swords.

fx.text: The pila punch through the shield wall and pin shields together. Men throw them away and fight unprotected. The legions charge downhill and drive the Helvetii back across the plain.
The pila break up their wall.

choices.label: Wait for them to reach you

fx.text: The shield wall reaches your line intact.

choices.label: Charge down before their shield wall can close up

decisions.title: Attack on the flank
decisions.text: As your lines follow the Helvetii, the Boii and Tulingi, about 15,000 strong, arrive and strike your exposed right flank.

hint.text: Your third line is behind the first two.

scout.text: Turn the third line round to face the new threat, while the first two press on.

choices.label: Turn the third line to face them

fx.text: Your third line wheels to meet the Boii and Tulingi while the first two keep driving the Helvetii.

choices.label: Halt the whole army and face every way at once

fx.text: The Boii crash into your flank.

decisions.title: The wagons
decisions.text: The Helvetii have fallen back to their wagons, where their families are. They fight on from behind them into the night.

hint.text: The fighting goes on in the dark.

scout.text: Storm the wagon laager; once it falls, the Helvetii cannot go on.

fx.text: The fighting at the wagons lasts into the night. At last the laager falls, with the Helvetii baggage. A son and daughter of Orgetorix are captured.
The Helvetii slip away in the night.
Your own grain is still short.
